items.stem: Which stage of a butterfly hatches from the egg?

explain.why: The adult is the last stage. The egg first hatches into a larva.
The pupa forms after the larva has grown; it does not hatch straight from the egg.
A nymph is a stage in the life cycle of a cockroach, not a butterfly.

solution: A butterfly's life cycle is egg, larva, pupa, adult.
The larva (caterpillar) hatches from the egg.

items.stem: How many stages are there in the life cycle of a frog?

explain.why: A frog has more than an egg and an adult; it also has a tadpole and a young frog.
Three stages (egg, young, adult) fits a cockroach or a chicken. A frog also has the tadpole and young frog stages.
A frog has no fifth stage. Its stages are egg, tadpole, young frog and adult.

solution: The stages of a frog are egg, tadpole, young frog and adult.
That makes four stages.

items.stem: Which of these animals has a pupa stage in its life cycle?

explain.why: A cockroach goes from egg to nymph to adult. It has no pupa.
A grasshopper goes from egg to nymph to adult. It has no pupa.
A chicken goes from egg to chick to adult. It has no pupa.

solution: A beetle's life cycle is egg, larva, pupa, adult.
The other three animals go from egg to a young that looks like the adult, so they have no pupa.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a mosquito. Which stage is missing in the box marked '?'

explain.why: A caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly. The larva of a mosquito is called a wriggler.
A tadpole is the young of a frog, not of a mosquito.
A nymph is found in insects with no pupa stage, such as the cockroach. A mosquito has a larva.

solution: The life cycle of a mosquito is egg, larva, pupa, adult.
The missing stage comes between the egg and the pupa, so it is the larva.

explain.why: A caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly.
A chick is the young of a chicken.
A nymph is the young of an insect such as a cockroach.

solution: The young of a frog that lives in water and has a tail but no legs is a tadpole.

items.stem: Which list shows the life cycle of a chicken in the correct order?

explain.why: Larva and pupa are stages of some insects. A chicken has neither.
The chick grows into the adult hen, so the adult comes last.
A chick hatches from an egg, so the egg comes first.

solution: A hen lays an egg. A chick hatches from the egg and grows into an adult hen.

options: Seed, adult plant, seedling, young plant
Seed, seedling, young plant, adult plant
Seed, seedling, adult plant, young plant
Seed, young plant, seedling, adult plant

explain.why: A seed cannot grow straight into an adult plant. It becomes a seedling first.
The plant grows from a young plant into an adult plant, not the other way round.
A seedling is the tiny plant that first grows out of the seed, so it comes before the young plant.

solution: The seed germinates and grows into a seedling.
The seedling grows into a young plant, then an adult plant.

items.stem: Which stage of a flowering plant makes the flowers that later form fruits with seeds?

explain.why: A seed has not started to grow yet, so it cannot make flowers.
A young plant is still growing. Flowers are made by the adult plant.
A seedling is too young to make flowers.

solution: Only the adult plant makes flowers.
The flowers form fruits that hold new seeds.

B shows the caterpillar (larva), which hatches from the egg.
C shows the adult butterfly.

solution: The egg is the first stage, which is shown by D.
The arrows go from D to the caterpillar (B), the pupa (A) and the adult (C).

explain.why: B shows the adult frog, which has four legs and no tail.
C shows the eggs, which are laid in a jelly-like mass.
D shows the young frog, which already has legs.

solution: The tadpole has a tail and no legs, so it is stage A.
It hatches from the eggs (C) and later grows into the young frog (D).

The egg hatches into the chick (A) first, not straight into the adult hen (B).
A is the chick. The chick hatches from the egg (C), so it cannot come before the egg.

solution: C is the egg, A is the chick and B is the adult hen.
Starting from the egg, the order is C, A, B.

explain.why: An egg does not feed.
A pupa does not feed. Its body is changing into the adult.
An adult butterfly sips nectar. It does not eat leaves or grow bigger.

solution: The larva (caterpillar) eats a lot of leaves and grows quickly.
The other stages either do not feed or feed on nectar.

A caterpillar crawls. It has no wings.

options: On dry leaves high in trees

explain.why: An adult mosquito bites people for blood, but she does not lay her eggs on their skin.
Mosquito eggs are laid where there is water, not in bird nests.
The eggs, larvae and pupae need water to develop, and dry leaves have none.

solution: Mosquito eggs hatch into larvae that live in water.
So the female lays her eggs in or near stagnant water.

A tadpole breathes with gills, which only work in water.
A tadpole swims with its tail and cannot live out of water.

solution: A tadpole has gills and a tail, so it lives in water.

A butterfly has four stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult.
A mosquito has four stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult.

solution: A cockroach goes from egg to nymph to adult.

items.stem: What do we call the stage between the larva and the adult in which an insect does not feed?

explain.why: The egg is the first stage, not the one between the larva and the adult.
A tadpole is a stage of a frog, not of an insect.
A nymph is a young stage of insects such as the cockroach. It feeds and comes before the adult.

solution: After feeding as a larva, the insect becomes a pupa.
The pupa does not feed while its body changes into the adult.

items.stem: Which statement about life cycles is correct?
options: Different living things can have different numbers of life cycle stages.
All animals have the same number of stages in their life cycles.
Plants and other living things that make seeds do not have a life cycle.
Only the animals that lay eggs are able to have a life cycle.

explain.why: A chicken has three stages, but a butterfly has four.
Plants have a life cycle too: seed, seedling, young plant and adult plant.
All living things have a life cycle, including plants and animals that do not lay eggs.

solution: A frog has four stages and a cockroach has three.
So different living things have different life cycles.

A chicken begins its life as an egg.
A cockroach begins its life as an egg in an egg case.

items.stem: The young of which animal looks like a small adult but has no wings?

explain.why: A mosquito larva lives in water and looks very different from the adult.
A beetle grub looks very different from the adult beetle.
A caterpillar looks very different from an adult butterfly.

solution: A cockroach nymph looks like a small adult without wings.
The young of the other three look very different from their adults.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a cockroach. What is the missing stage?

explain.why: A tadpole is a stage of a frog.
A cockroach has no pupa stage.
The young of a cockroach is called a nymph, not a larva.

The egg, larva and pupa live in water.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a mosquito. Which letter shows the adult mosquito?

explain.why: B shows the larva that hangs below the water surface.
C shows the eggs floating on the water.
D shows the pupa.

solution: The adult mosquito has wings and long legs, which are shown by A.
The other three stages live in water.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a beetle. Which letter shows the pupa?

explain.why: A shows the larva (grub), which feeds and grows.
C shows the eggs.
D shows the adult beetle.

solution: The pupa comes after the larva and before the adult, so it is stage B.
The arrows go from the eggs (C) to the grub (A), the pupa (B) and the adult (D).

items.stem: A student watched a butterfly pupa for several days. What did the pupa do during this time?
options: It ate leaves to grow bigger.
It flew from plant to plant.
It did not feed and hardly moved.

explain.why: Eating leaves is what the larva does before it becomes a pupa.
Only the adult butterfly drinks nectar.
The pupa has no working wings, so it cannot fly.

solution: The pupa is a stage in which the insect does not feed.
Its body changes into the adult inside, and it hardly moves.

items.stem: Which statement about the larva of a mosquito is correct?
options: It lives in water and does not feed.
It lives on land and drinks blood.
It has wings and can fly.
It lives in water and feeds on tiny living things.

explain.why: The larva feeds and grows. It is the pupa that does not feed.
The larva lives in water. Only the adult female drinks blood.
Only the adult mosquito has wings.

solution: A mosquito larva (wriggler) lives in water and feeds on tiny living things to grow.
Wings and blood-feeding belong to the adult.

items.stem: Which pair of animals both have a pupa stage?

explain.why: A cockroach goes from egg to nymph to adult, so it has no pupa.
A grasshopper has no pupa. It goes from egg to nymph to adult.
A frog has a tadpole and a young frog, but no pupa.

solution: A mosquito goes from egg to larva to pupa to adult.
A beetle does too. The other animals in the options each lack a pupa.

items.stem: Which pair of animals both have young that look similar to the adult?

explain.why: A mosquito larva looks very different from the adult mosquito.
A beetle grub looks very different from the adult beetle.
A caterpillar and a tadpole both look very different from their adults.

solution: A cockroach nymph and a chick both look like smaller versions of the adult.
The larvae and tadpoles in the other pairs look very different from their adults.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a frog. Which are the missing stages, in order?

explain.why: Larva and pupa are insect stages. A frog is not an insect.
A nymph is an insect stage. The young of a frog is a tadpole.
The tadpole has no legs. It grows legs and becomes the young frog afterwards.

solution: An egg hatches into a tadpole.
The tadpole grows legs and becomes a young frog, which then grows into the adult frog.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a butterfly. Which letter shows the stage that comes just before the adult?

C is the adult butterfly itself.
D is the egg, which is the first stage.

solution: The arrows go from the egg (D) to the caterpillar (B), the pupa (A) and then the adult (C).
The stage just before the adult is the pupa, A.

B is the adult frog, which comes after the young frog.
C shows the eggs, which come before the tadpole.

solution: The arrows go from the eggs (C) to the tadpole (A) and then to the young frog (D).

C is the nymph. The egg (B) has to come first.
A is the adult. The list must start from the egg, which is B.

solution: B is the egg in the soil, C is the nymph and A is the adult.
Starting from the egg, the order is B, C, A.

The table correctly shows the tadpole and young frog stages of a frog.

The other three rows are correct.

items.stem: Which stage of a cockroach eats the same kind of food as the adult cockroach?

explain.why: An egg does not feed.
A cockroach has a nymph, not a larva.
A cockroach has no pupa stage.

solution: The nymph looks like a small adult and eats similar food to it.
A cockroach has no larva or pupa.

items.stem: A caterpillar eats many leaves. Then it stops eating and hangs from a twig. Which stage does it become next?

explain.why: The caterpillar becomes a pupa first. The adult emerges from the pupa.
The egg is the first stage. The caterpillar has already hatched from it.
A nymph is a stage of insects such as the cockroach, not of the butterfly.

solution: After feeding, the larva stops eating and becomes a pupa.
The adult butterfly comes out of the pupa later.

items.stem: Which statement about a tadpole and an adult frog is correct?
options: A tadpole and an adult frog both breathe with gills.
A tadpole breathes with lungs and lives on land.
A tadpole has four legs, but an adult frog has none.
A tadpole has gills and a tail, but an adult frog has lungs and legs.

explain.why: An adult frog breathes with lungs and through its skin.
A tadpole lives in water and breathes with gills.
A tadpole has no legs at first. The adult frog has four.

solution: A tadpole lives in water and breathes with gills. It has a tail and no legs.
An adult frog has lungs and four legs.

items.stem: A cockroach nymph moults several times. Why does it do so?
options: To grow bigger, because its hard outer skin cannot stretch.
To find food in a new place.

explain.why: A cockroach has no pupa stage. A nymph moults into a bigger nymph, and finally an adult.
Only the adult lays eggs, and moulting does not do that.
Moulting is about growing, not about finding food.

solution: The hard outer skin of a nymph does not stretch.
The nymph sheds it (moults) so that it can grow bigger.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a flowering plant. Which stage belongs in the box marked '?'

explain.why: A fruit is part of the adult plant. It holds seeds but is not a stage between seedling and adult.
A larva is an insect stage, not a plant stage.
Flowering plants grow from seeds, not eggs.

solution: A seed grows into a seedling, then a young plant.
The young plant grows into the adult plant with flowers.

items.stem: Which of these is a difference between the life cycles of a frog and a bean plant?
options: A frog starts as an egg, but a bean plant starts as a seed.
A bean plant has an adult stage, but a frog does not.
A frog grows bigger, but a bean plant stays the same size.
A frog has stages, but a bean plant does not.

explain.why: Both of them grow into adults.
A bean plant also grows bigger as it develops.
A bean plant also has stages: seed, seedling, young plant and adult plant.

solution: A frog begins as an egg that is laid in water.
A bean plant begins as a seed. Both then grow through stages into adults.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a beetle. Which two letters show stages in which the beetle does not feed?

explain.why: A is the larva (grub), which feeds a lot.
Both the larva (A) and the adult (D) feed.
D is the adult beetle, which feeds.

solution: The pupa (B) and the eggs (C) do not feed.
The larva (A) and adult beetle (D) feed.

figure.alt: Life cycle of a beetle drawn as a ring of four stages joined by arrows, marked A to D.

items.stem: The graph shows how many days a certain butterfly spent in each stage. How many days did it spend as a larva and a pupa together?

explain.why: 14 days is the time as a larva only. The pupa stage must be added.
28 days includes the 4 days of the egg stage as well.
48 days is the total for all four stages.

solution: The larva stage lasted 14 days and the pupa stage lasted 10 days.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a chicken. Which letter shows the stage that is able to lay eggs?

explain.why: A is the chick, which is too young to lay eggs.
C is the egg, which cannot lay eggs.
The chick (A) cannot lay eggs. Only the adult hen (B) can.

solution: Only the adult hen can lay eggs.
The adult hen is stage B.

figure.alt: Life cycle of a chicken drawn as a ring of three stages joined by arrows, marked A to C.

items.stem: Why is stagnant water in a flower pot plate a problem?
options: Mosquitoes lay eggs only in fast-flowing drains.
Adult mosquitoes need to drink the water to grow.
The water turns mosquito larvae into caterpillars.
Mosquitoes can lay eggs there, and the larvae and pupae live in the water.

explain.why: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water such as water in pot plates.
Adult mosquitoes do not grow. The young stages grow in the water.
Caterpillars are young butterflies. Mosquito larvae are wrigglers.

solution: The eggs, larvae and pupae of a mosquito develop in water.
Stagnant water gives the mosquitoes a place to breed.

items.stem: A student plants a green bean seed and watches it for several weeks. Which list shows what she will see, in order?
options: Seed, young plant, seedling with small leaves, adult plant with flowers
Seed, seedling with small leaves, young plant, adult plant with flowers
Seed, adult plant with flowers, seedling with small leaves, young plant
Seedling with small leaves, seed, young plant, adult plant with flowers

explain.why: The seedling is the first small plant that grows from the seed, so it comes before the young plant.
The plant cannot flower before it has grown from a seedling.
The seed has to be there before it can grow into a seedling.

solution: The seed grows into a seedling with small leaves.
The seedling becomes a young plant and then an adult plant that makes flowers.

items.stem: Which animal belongs in the overlap of the diagram, marked '?'

explain.why: A grasshopper has no pupa and its young do not live in water.
A cockroach has no pupa and its young do not live in water.
A chicken has no pupa and its young do not live in water.

solution: The overlap needs an animal with a pupa stage whose young also live in water.
Only the mosquito does both.

items.stem: Its eggs hatch into young that look like small adults without wings. The young moult several times and grow wings. Which animal is this?

explain.why: A mosquito's young lives in water and looks very different from the adult.
A butterfly's young is a caterpillar, which looks nothing like the adult.
A beetle's young is a grub, which does not look like the adult.

solution: Young that look like small adults and have no pupa stage point to a cockroach.
The other animals have larvae that look very different from the adults.

items.stem: How is the life cycle of a chicken different from that of a butterfly?
options: A chicken has no pupa stage, but a butterfly has one.
A chicken has more stages than a butterfly.
A chicken has no egg stage, but a butterfly has one.
The young of a chicken look different from the adult, but the young of a butterfly look the same.

explain.why: A chicken has three stages and a butterfly has four.
Both animals begin as eggs.
It is the other way round. A chick looks like the adult, but a caterpillar does not.

solution: A chicken goes from egg to chick to adult, which is three stages.
A butterfly has four stages, including the pupa.

items.stem: Which of these is the same for the life cycles of the butterfly and the frog?
options: Their young look very different from the adults.
Both lay their eggs in water.

explain.why: Each has four stages.
A frog has no pupa stage.
A butterfly lays its eggs on leaves, not in water.

solution: A caterpillar looks very different from a butterfly, and a tadpole looks very different from a frog.
Both life cycles have four stages, but only the butterfly has a pupa.

items.stem: A farmer found the insect in the picture eating the leaves of his vegetables. At which stage of its life cycle is the insect?

explain.why: A pupa does not feed.
The adult has wings and does not eat leaves.
A nymph looks like a small adult and belongs to insects with no pupa stage. This insect looks nothing like an adult.

solution: The insect has a soft worm-like body, feeds on leaves and has no wings.
This is the larva stage.

figure.alt: A vegetable leaf with holes in it and a soft, worm-like insect with several pairs of legs feeding on the leaf.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a cockroach. Which letter shows the stage that hatches from the egg case?

explain.why: B shows the egg case itself.
C shows the adult cockroach, which comes after the nymph.
Neither the egg case (B) nor the adult (C) hatches from the egg case.

solution: The egg case hatches into a nymph.
The nymph is stage A. It looks like a small adult without wings.

figure.alt: Life cycle of a cockroach drawn as a ring of three stages joined by arrows, marked A to C.

items.stem: The table shows four stages in the life cycle of animal X. Which animal is X?

explain.why: The young frog (stage 3) feeds, but the table says stage 3 does not feed.
The eggs, larvae and pupae of a beetle do not live in water.
The eggs of a butterfly are laid on leaves, not in water, so stage 1 would not be in water.

solution: Stage 1 (egg) and stage 3 (pupa) do not feed, and stages 1 to 3 live in water.
The larva (stage 2) feeds and the pupa moves but does not feed. Only a mosquito fits.

items.stem: Which statement correctly compares a cockroach and a butterfly?
options: The young of a cockroach look like the adult, but the young of a butterfly do not.
Both have a pupa stage before becoming adults.
A butterfly has three stages, but a cockroach has four.
The adult cockroach lays eggs, but the adult butterfly does not.

explain.why: A cockroach has no pupa stage.
It is the other way round. A cockroach has three stages and a butterfly has four.
Both adults lay eggs.

solution: A cockroach nymph looks like a small adult.
A caterpillar looks very different from the adult butterfly.

items.stem: Which animal has the same number of stages in its life cycle as a beetle?

explain.why: A cockroach has three stages.
A grasshopper has three stages.
A chicken has three stages.

solution: A beetle has four stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult.
A frog also has four: egg, tadpole, young frog and adult.
The others have three stages each.

items.stem: Which of these correctly matches each animal to its young?
options: Frog: tadpole, beetle: grub, cockroach: nymph
Frog: tadpole, beetle: nymph, cockroach: grub
Frog: grub, beetle: tadpole, cockroach: nymph
Frog: nymph, beetle: grub, cockroach: tadpole

explain.why: The young of a beetle is a grub (larva) and the young of a cockroach is a nymph. These two are swapped.
The young of a frog is a tadpole and the young of a beetle is a grub. These two are swapped.
The young of a frog is a tadpole and the young of a cockroach is a nymph. These two are swapped.

solution: A frog's young is a tadpole, a beetle's young is a grub (larva) and a cockroach's young is a nymph.

items.stem: The picture shows the plate under a flower pot at a home in Singapore. It holds some water. Which action best stops mosquitoes from breeding here?
options: Empty the water and scrub the plate every week
Put on mosquito repellent when going outside
Keep the windows closed at all times
Switch on a fan near the flower pot

explain.why: Repellent protects a person from bites but does nothing to stop mosquitoes breeding.
This keeps adults out of the house but does not stop breeding in the water.
A fan may blow adults away, but eggs, larvae and pupae still develop in the water.

solution: Mosquito eggs, larvae and pupae develop in water.
Removing the water and scrubbing off any eggs breaks the life cycle.

figure.alt: A flower pot standing in a plate that holds a little water, seen from the side.

items.stem: The table shows the least number of days a mosquito spends at each stage in water. Eggs are laid in a plate of water. What is the earliest number of days after which an adult mosquito can come out of the water?

explain.why: 4 days is the egg and pupa stages only. The larva stage has been left out.
5 days is the larva stage only. The egg and pupa stages must be added.
7 days adds the egg and larva stages but leaves out the 2 days of the pupa.

solution: The egg lasts at least 2 days, the larva 5 days and the pupa 2 days.

items.stem: A student says that emptying the water from a pot plate every 7 days helps to stop mosquitoes. Using the table, which statement best explains why?
options: Adult mosquitoes drink all of the water in the pot plate in 7 days.
No adult comes out in under 9 days, so the eggs, larvae and pupae are removed first.
Mosquito eggs take 7 days to hatch, so only the eggs are in the water until then.
The pupae change back into larvae after 7 days in the water.

explain.why: Adult mosquitoes do not use up the water in a pot plate.
The table shows that eggs take at least 2 days, and larvae and pupae follow.
A pupa changes into an adult, never back into a larva.

solution: The table shows that an adult needs at least 2 + 5 + 2 = 9 days.
If the water is emptied within 7 days, the eggs, larvae and pupae are thrown away before any adult comes out.

items.stem: Which statement about the pupa stage is correct?
options: The pupa lays eggs for the next life cycle.
The pupa feeds a lot so that it can grow bigger.
The pupa is the same as the nymph of a cockroach.
The pupa does not feed, but its body changes into that of the adult.

explain.why: Only the adult lays eggs.
Feeding and growing is what the larva does.
A nymph feeds and looks like a small adult. A pupa does not feed and looks different.

solution: The pupa is a stage in which the insect does not feed.
Inside it, the body changes into the body of the adult.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a mosquito. Which letters show the stages that live in water?

explain.why: A is the adult mosquito, which flies in the air.
A is the adult mosquito, which flies in the air.
A is the adult mosquito, which flies in the air.

solution: The eggs (C), larva (B) and pupa (D) all live in water.
The adult (A) is the only stage that lives in the air.

figure.alt: Life cycle of a mosquito drawn as a ring of four stages joined by arrows, marked A to D.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a frog. Which letters show stages that have a tail?

explain.why: B is the adult frog, which has no tail.
The adult frog (B) has no tail, and the eggs (C) have not grown a tail you can see.
The eggs (C) have no tail you can see.

solution: The tadpole (A) has a long tail.
The young frog (D) still has a short tail that gets smaller as it grows.

figure.alt: Life cycle of a frog drawn as a ring of four stages joined by arrows, marked A to D.

items.stem: Which statement about the grub of a beetle is correct?
options: It is the nymph, which looks like a small adult beetle.
It is the pupa, which does not feed.
It is the adult, which lays the eggs.
It is the larva, which feeds a lot before it changes into a pupa.

explain.why: A beetle has no nymph stage. Its young does not look like the adult.
The pupa comes after the grub and does not feed.
The grub is a young stage. Only the adult beetle lays eggs.

solution: A beetle grub is the larva stage.
It feeds a lot, grows, and later becomes a pupa.

items.stem: A student finds a young insect. Which observation shows that it is a nymph and not a larva?
options: It stops eating and forms a case around itself.
It looks like a smaller adult, but its wings are not fully grown.
It looks very different from the adult.
It will become a pupa next.

explain.why: This is what a larva does before it becomes a pupa.
A young insect that looks very different from the adult is a larva.
Only a larva becomes a pupa. A nymph becomes an adult.

solution: A nymph looks like a small adult, so it does not look very different.
A larva looks very different and becomes a pupa.

items.stem: Which statement about the mosquito and the frog is correct?
options: Both have four stages, and their young live in water.
Only the frog has four stages in its life cycle.
Only the mosquito's young live in water.

explain.why: A mosquito has four stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult.
Tadpoles live in water too.
A frog has no pupa. It has a tadpole and a young frog.

solution: A mosquito has four stages and a frog has four stages.
The young of both live in water.

items.stem: Which list contains only animals whose young look very different from the adult?

explain.why: A cockroach nymph looks like a small adult.
A grasshopper nymph looks like a small adult.
A chick looks like a small adult.

solution: A caterpillar, a tadpole and a grub all look very different from the adult.
Each of the other lists has an animal with young that looks like the adult.

items.stem: Jun Wei says that all insects have a pupa stage. Which animal shows that he is wrong?

explain.why: A beetle is an insect with a pupa stage, so it does not show he is wrong.
A butterfly is an insect with a pupa stage, so it does not show he is wrong.
A mosquito is an insect with a pupa stage, so it does not show he is wrong.

solution: A cockroach is an insect that goes from egg to nymph to adult.
It has no pupa stage, so Jun Wei is wrong.

items.stem: A student measured the height of a bean plant every 2 weeks. During which period did the plant grow the fastest?

explain.why: The plant grew only 4 cm in this period.
The plant grew 8 cm in this period, which is less than in weeks 4 to 6.
The plant grew 12 cm in this period, which is less than in weeks 4 to 6.

solution: From week 4 to week 6 the height went from 12 cm to 30 cm, a growth of 18 cm.
That is more than in any other period.

options: A chick stops growing, but a butterfly larva keeps on growing.
A chick looks like a small adult, but a butterfly larva does not.
A chick hatches from a seed, but a butterfly larva hatches from an egg.
A chick is an adult chicken, but a butterfly larva is a young animal.

explain.why: A chick keeps growing until it becomes an adult hen.
A chick hatches from an egg.
A chick is the young of a chicken.

solution: A chick looks like a smaller version of the adult hen.
A butterfly larva (caterpillar) looks very different from the adult butterfly.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a butterfly. Stage D is the adult. Which letter shows the pupa?

explain.why: A is the stage that comes just after the adult, which is the egg.
B is the stage after the egg, which is the larva.
D is the adult butterfly.

solution: The arrows go clockwise from A to B to C to D and back to A.
D is the adult, so A is the egg, B is the larva and C is the pupa.

options: The larva and pupa should be replaced by one stage called the nymph.
The adult should come before the egg.
The pupa should come before the larva.
The egg stage should be removed because cockroaches give birth to young.

explain.why: The adult lays the eggs, but the life cycle of a cockroach starts from the egg.
A pupa never comes before a larva, and a cockroach has neither.
A cockroach starts its life as an egg.

solution: A cockroach goes from egg to nymph to adult.
It has no larva or pupa stage.

items.stem: The table shows how a student sorted six animals into two groups. Which feature did she use to sort them?
options: Whether the young look like the adult
Whether the life cycle has four stages
Whether the animal has a pupa stage
Whether the young live in water

explain.why: A frog's young does not look like the adult, but the frog is in Group P with the cockroach and chicken.
The frog has four stages but is in Group P with the cockroach and chicken, which have three.
Both the frog (Group P) and the mosquito (Group Q) have young that live in water.

explain.why: C is wrong. A cockroach has no pupa stage.
C is wrong. A cockroach has no pupa stage.

solution: A and B are correct. The nymph looks like a small adult and its wings are not fully grown.
C is wrong because a cockroach has no pupa.

explain.why: B is wrong. A butterfly larva has no wings.
B is wrong. A butterfly larva has no wings.

solution: A and C are correct. The caterpillar eats leaves and moults as it grows bigger.
B is wrong because wings belong to the adult.

explain.why: P has a tail but no legs, so it is the tadpole.
R has four legs and no tail, so it is the adult frog.
S has neither legs nor a tail, so it is the egg.

solution: The young frog has four legs and still has a short tail.
Only stage Q has both.

items.stem: Which statement about the life cycles of living things is correct?
options: Adults of the same kind produce young that go through the same stages.
Every stage of a life cycle lasts the same number of days.
All living things begin their life cycles as eggs.
Every young animal looks like its parents when it hatches.

explain.why: A chicken egg takes about three weeks to hatch, but a hen lives for years, so stages differ in length.
A flowering plant begins its life cycle as a seed.
A caterpillar and a tadpole look very different from their parents.

solution: Adults of the same kind lay eggs or make seeds that grow into new adults.
The young go through the same stages as their parents did.

items.stem: Which of these is true for the chicken and the cockroach, but not for the frog?
options: Their life cycles begin with an egg.
Their young look like smaller versions of the adult.
Their life cycles have an adult stage.

explain.why: This is also true for the frog, so it does not tell them apart.
This is also true for the frog, so it does not tell them apart.
Neither the chick nor the nymph lives in water.

solution: A chick and a cockroach nymph look like small adults.
A tadpole does not look like the adult frog.

items.stem: The diagram shows the life cycle of a flowering plant. Which shows the stages in the correct order, starting from the seed?

explain.why: A is the adult plant. The list must start from the seed, which is B.
A is the adult plant, which is the last stage and not the second.
D is the young plant. It comes after the seedling (C), not before.

solution: B is the seed, C is the seedling, D is the young plant and A is the adult plant.
Starting from the seed, the order is B, C, D, A.
